descs.en: He thinks her hands are broken and opens every door for her. She secretly got her surgeon’s hands back, and works nights in a basement as the family’s ghost surgeon.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Elara Lin is a final-year medical student who talks all the time, practises stitches on bananas, and on her first morning on the surgical ward tells the chief resident he's missed a leak. She's right. By the end of the day Wang Xing Yue has handed her logbook to someone else, so that he can ask her to dinner. He's been in love with her for fifteen months. The only person he's told is his brother, who sent him a paper about voles.

She's also the Lins' surgeon. When the family's people bleed somewhere a hospital can't see them, she goes, with whatever she can steal. In a supply room at three in the morning she begs him not to ask, and he promises he won't. He keeps that promise for three and a half years: through a knife at her father's door that cuts through her right wrist, a winter when she stops talking, and the year she gets her hands back in secret on a machine in a garage and goes back to work in a cellar, in a mask, as Doctor Ghost.

He's known since she mended his pillowcase at two in the morning. He never asks her to stop. He restocks her bag instead, and when she finally calls him, he comes with blood.

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Elara has been in the corner of every Lin book so far: late, in scrubs, with her hair falling out of its clip, crying at weddings, stapling somebody's head on a kitchen table. I wanted to know what all that cost her, and who looks after the person who looks after everyone.

Xing Yue isn't a nice man to anyone but her. He makes residents sick on his ward rounds, he checks her location, he goes through her bag, and he lies to his own professor without blinking. I didn't want the book to tell him off for any of it. The one thing he never does is ask her to be someone else, and that felt like the most romantic thing I could give her.

There's blood, because it's a book about surgeons, but the medicine stays at story level. The love scenes are slow and mostly come after night shifts, in early light, which is how she likes them. Nobody has a baby. They get a house with a long kitchen, two pagers, a phone in a drawer that rings at half past eleven, and each other.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers. Mature themes and heated love scenes.

This is a 21+ medical romance, warm and funny for most of its length, but it has some hard moments:

• Love scenes throughout, heated and detailed but not explicit, from She Narrates Everything on

• An infected knife wound treated over the phone at night (Three in the Morning, on Speaker)

• A gunshot wound, sepsis and surgery on a kitchen table, with stolen hospital supplies (Zhao Zhendong Is Bleeding Out, Fifteen Days of Drips)

• A shooting in a noodle shop and a head wound closed at home (Staples on a Kitchen Table)

• A people-smuggling boat and cold, frightened survivors at a border bridge (The Seventh Guest)

• Burns after a workshop fire (Again?)

• A knife attack, heavy bleeding and a serious hand injury (The Knife at the Red Door)

• Nerve pain, withdrawal into silence, and a father's confession to a crime that killed her birth parents in a fire (The House Is Too Quiet, A Name in a Ledger, Elara Before the Lins)

• A prison visit (Her Mother's Window)

• Secret surgery outside hospitals, falsified records and lies to police and employers (A Surgeon Who Doesn't Exist, The Cellar Under the Rope Store, Doctor Ghost)

• A girl's face cut with a bottle by her father, mentioned (The Cellar Under the Rope Store)

• A gunshot to the thigh and life-threatening bleeding (Two Surgeons, One Table)

• A workplace inquiry and suspension (I Know)

• A footbridge collapse with many casualties (A Mass Casualty Night)

• A partner who tracks her phone and goes through her bag, shown without judgement (from Three in the Morning, on Speaker)

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
City Hospital — the teaching hospital at the foot of the hill. Ward 9B, general surgery, is on the ninth floor of the tower; the old 1930s block stands behind it.
Harbourside General — the big hospital by the harbour, where Elara does her intern year and goes back to training in 2027.
The Crestview — the private hospital on the hill above the old racecourse, where Dr. Meng repairs her hand and Ms. Cui makes her cry.
The hospital garden — behind the old block: a camphor tree older than the hospital, a koi pond, and the fourth window along on the first floor, which was her mother's ward.
14 Banyan Terrace — his flat, the top two floors and roof of a white 1950s building ten minutes downhill from City Hospital.
2 Camphor Hill — the old doctor's house above the hospital, with a long kitchen and a back room for the rig. Bought in both their names, without asking.
The Walled City — the old district where the Lins live, behind a red door with a brass fish knocker and eleven chairs that don't match.
The cellar under the rope store — the room Raiden builds next to the garage near the Docks, behind a steel door painted to look like wood.
Doctor Ghost — the name the docks give the masked surgeon who never speaks and always hums.
The rig — Jinx's steel training machine for Elara's hand: springs, a pinch gauge, pins and a wire that buzzes. Every knob turns a quarter.
The ghost phone — the line that rings only from her father's or Uncle Mok's numbers. From July 2027 it lives in the kitchen drawer.
The dot — her phone location, shared with him ‘for night shifts’ from 2023, and his with her from 2026.
The rules — what they wrote on the back of his suspension letter. Rule one: nobody does this alone.
Qu Xiaoyue — her birth name, ‘little moon’. Elara is a moon of Jupiter, so she kept a piece of it.
Qu Lighterage — her father's firm: four lighter boats between the ships and the old Walled City piers.
Plum Steps — the children's home at the top of a long flight of stone steps, closed in 2011.
Loupes — magnifying glasses surgeons wear to operate. Hers are dark red, made for her eyes, with E.L. inside the arm.
Registrar, consultant — a registrar is a mid-level surgeon in training; a consultant is the senior surgeon in charge.
